name: Celiac Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ACG Guidelines / ESPGHAN 2020 Criteria for Celiac Disease

criteria.description: Positive tissue transglutaminase IgA (tTG-IgA) antibody (>10x upper limit of normal in ESPGHAN pediatric criteria allows biopsy-free diagnosis)
Positive deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies (DGP-IgG) - especially useful in IgA-deficient patients
Duodenal biopsy showing villous atrophy (Marsh 3), crypt hyperplasia, and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes
Clinical and serologic improvement on gluten-free diet
HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 positivity (nearly 100% of celiac patients carry one or both)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Positive serology (tTG-IgA) plus confirmatory duodenal biopsy (Marsh 3) in adults; in children, tTG-IgA >10x ULN plus positive EMA on separate sample can be biopsy-free
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Patient must be on a gluten-containing diet at time of testing. IgA-deficient patients (2-3% of celiac patients) need IgG-based testing. Negative HLA-DQ2/DQ8 essentially excludes celiac disease.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Villous atrophy with crypt hyperplasia on duodenal biopsy (Marsh 3)
pathognomonic.notes: Must be on gluten-containing diet; at least 4-6 biopsies from duodenum including bulb
Intensely pruritic papulovesicular rash on extensor surfaces; granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae; pathognomonic for celiac disease

rare.notes: Associated with refractory celiac disease type II

laboratory: Total IgA level (to exclude IgA deficiency)
Iron deficiency anemia (low ferritin, low iron, elevated TIBC)
imaging: CT/MRI enterography: small bowel wall thickening, jejunal fold reversal (jejunization of ileum), mesenteric lymphadenopathy
Video capsule endoscopy: villous atrophy, scalloping of duodenal folds
genetic: HLA-DQ2.5 (DQA1*05:01/DQB1*02:01) present in ~90% of celiac patients
Absence of HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 has >99% negative predictive value
other: Upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies: villous atrophy (Marsh-Oberhuber classification), crypt hyperplasia, increased IELs (>25/100 enterocytes)
Skin biopsy (dermatitis herpetiformis): granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae on direct immunofluorescence

distinguishingFeatures: Can affect any part of GI tract
History of travel to endemic area

redFlags: Failure to improve on strict gluten-free diet after 6-12 months (consider refractory celiac disease)
Recurrent symptoms after initial improvement (dietary non-adherence vs. refractory disease)
New alarm symptoms (significant weight loss, GI bleeding) suggesting lymphoma
Unexplained iron deficiency anemia refractory to supplementation
Dermatitis herpetiformis not responding to dapsone and GFD
references: Rubio-Tapia A, et al. ACG Clinical Guidelines: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease. Am J Gastroenterol. 2023;118(1):59-76.
Husby S, et al. European Society Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition Guidelines for Diagnosing Coeliac Disease 2020. J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr. 2020;70(1):141-156.
Lebwohl B, et al. Celiac disease. Lancet. 2018;391(10115):70-81.
